rows.label: White Terror and local royalist violence after Thermidor
rows.source_grounded_note: White Terror: pages291–293,327 support political retaliation, identifiable royalist companies, mostly local vengeance, imprisonment making victims vulnerable, official connivance, regional death estimates and continuing fragmented violence. Essential is justified as a sustained source argument about reaction and the failure of revolutionary reconciliation. Parent should name the prison-massacre mechanism and contrast the Companies of the Sun/Jesus with uncoordinated vendettas; these are not all one centralized royalist programme. Current evidence correctly qualifies the approximate2000south-eastern victims in1795 and does not invent a majority afterMay. Later observers’ claims about local aims remain attributed, not proof that no royalist connections existed.

rows.label: Jacobins under the Directory: repeated revival, containment and repression
rows.source_grounded_note: Directorial Jacobins: pages324–325,335–336,371–373 substantiate distinct cycles of press/club revival and official encouragement, then restriction, alongside the1799 emergency measures and Sieyes’s executive project. Major warranted. Main should name the concrete1799 conscription/loan/hostages agenda and containment through Manège closure and defeat of Country in Danger, not leave all policy content as hidden facets. Pantheon, constitutional circles and Manège must remain distinct; previous Jacobin association does not prove Babouvist conspiracy. Source locators and current qualifications are supportable. In1799 official containment also served Sieyes’s projected constitutional change, beyond preservation of an abstract centre.

rows.label: Directory: political balance, loss of legitimacy and collapse
rows.source_grounded_note: Directory: complete318–340source reread from the prior actual component pass plus369,375–377 support the political pendulum, dependence on force, financial alienation, discounted elections and failure to acknowledge legitimate opposition or organize a centre. Essential warranted. Main should explicitly retain failure to build its own moderate party and mutually intolerant opposition, while not blaming constitutional mechanics alone. EVID-SUCC-779DB40E1DE7 at369 is valid in content but incorrectly tagged CHUNK-014/localC014 despite physical CHUNK-016; rebind chapter metadata and incorporate369 into the appropriate treatment/facet source pages. Add328 to the first treatment/facet for the already retained paired-trial evidence. Source340’s forecast of military abandonment is a conclusion, not an assertion of an already completed coup.

rows.label: Sister republics: creation, constitutional diversity and constrained sovereignty
rows.source_grounded_note: Sister republics: pages338–339,343–344,346–347,355,361–364 support a comparative institutional requirement distinct from the wider Great Nation interpretation. Major warranted. The main fields appropriately preserve degrees of local initiative and French constraint. Evidence/treatment pages currently omit344/346–347for Dutch elected constitutional life and domestic autonomy, although those claims are required in the parent; add direct eligible evidence. Ligurian local drafting/plebiscite is on362 and can be made explicit in that existing summary alongside the separate Roman supremacy claim. Cisalpine constitution/nomination on361 supplies another distinct comparison and should have direct support if retained. Do not treat the qualifier about Dutch initial sympathizers as proof that no individual collaborators existed elsewhere. The Directory’s reluctance toward Naples remains explicit.

rows.label: Great Nation: territorial expansion, liberation claims and coercive hegemony
rows.source_grounded_note: Great Nation: pages337–339,353–354,361,368 support exclusive French conceptions of liberty, differentiated annexations/client rule, extraction and waning foreign support. Essential warranted. Retire EVID-SUCC-36A53E4C9D0D and map345-derived treatment/facet requirements under source-scope-disposition.v3; caption topic does not substantiate its internal political categories. Eligible prose on348 and361–362 independently supports distinctions between annexation and client institutions; add appropriate direct support instead of relabeling map evidence. Existing353/361historical evidence needs corresponding treatment/facet page inclusion. Source368 locates defeat and collapse inItaly in1799; avoid implying that all sister republics everywhere disappeared then. Preserve recognition of native collaborators and reforms rather than absolute nullification of change.

rows.label: War finance through conquest: extraction, army dependence and occupied economies
rows.source_grounded_note: War finance through conquest: pages333,347–348,352,355,358,363 support systemic extraction, foreign coin as an important state resource, dependence on commanders, local requisitions/indemnities/art and discriminatory tariffs. Major warranted, distinct from institutional autonomy and general hegemony. Main/stance correctly reject an explanation confined to personal corruption. The parent qualifier about later recovery is source-supported by350forBelgian industry but not currently evidenced; add350 and make the country/time qualification explicit, not a universal recovery claim. Preserve the distinction between French constraints and British blockade in Dutch economic damage. Current evidence summaries otherwise fit their pages.

rows.label: Jourdan Law: conscription, institutionalization and resistance
rows.source_grounded_note: Jourdan Law: pages340,371,373–374,384 support annual age classes, initial preference for volunteers, full1799 call-up without purchase of substitutes, evasion and insurgent/criminal recruitment. Major warranted as a distinct institutional change. Main phrase without easy substitution is weaker than the actual full-activation prohibition: specify that purchase of substitutes was prohibited for the1799call. EVID-SUCC-7D0098214957 should say eligible20–25year-olds, not an unbounded universal conscription claim. The parent correctly separates this law from Hostages/forced-loan repeal; page384 supplies continuing evasion and later easing of pressure rather than a repeal claim.

rows.label: Bonaparte’s departure from Egypt, return and coup alliance
rows.source_grounded_note: Bonaparte return: pages368,374 support pessimism and delayed information, secret departure before receipt of an already-issued evacuation order, public acclaim and tactical coup alliance. Major warranted. EVID-SUCC-260DA72F340A should distinguish the army left behind from the remnants depleted by two-thirds at surrender two years later; avoid placing the later depletion wholly at departure. The main fields already preserve separate actors’ expectations and the return’s preparatory role. The source says he left before receiving orders, not that the Directory had never issued any. No automatic equation of public acclaim with informed approval of abandoning the army.

rows.label: Concordat: negotiated settlement, papal revival and lasting polarization
rows.source_grounded_note: Concordat: pages386–390,398,424 support difficult bilateral negotiation, religious freedom, paid state-nominated hierarchy, nonrestitution, new episcopate, unilateral Organic Articles, papal gains and lasting polarization. Essential warranted; main is substantially coherent. EVID-SUCC-C319956F5ED9 at398 supports trauma and incomplete reconciliation but not the specific claim about every constitutional priest; narrow it or separately ground the constitutional-bishop issue in388. EVID-C319956F5ED9 and DABA28C566DA are physically CHUNK-017 yet tagged CHUNK-016; rebind source chapter metadata to the retrospective treatment and add424 to its pages. Add390 to the first treatment/facet for promulgation evidence. Main should explicitly distinguish the unilateral Organic Articles’ restrictions from terms mutually agreed, and the first article’s majority faith from exclusive state religion. Preserve389’s chronology problem in auxiliary controls without rewriting the source.

rows.label: Peace of Campo Formio and the end of the continental war
rows.source_grounded_note: Campo Formio: pages217–218,332 support the Austrian peace, Venetian partition, recognition of Belgian/Rhine/Italian arrangements, deferred imperial redistribution and continued British war. Essential is defensible as the chapter’s continental-war settlement, not a named-treaty quota. Main should incorporate the post-Fructidor elimination of Austrian hopes of exploiting French division, currently hidden in the added treatment. Austrian recognition did not bind the HolyRomanEmpire; this limiting distinction and futureRastadtcompensation should remain clear. Source dates and terms are otherwise correctly represented.

rows.label: Lille negotiations, Fructidor, and the hardening of French peace terms
rows.source_grounded_note: Lille: pages200,202,211–212,215–218,330,332 read against the complete record. Major warranted for negotiation and political interference, but copied broad Pittwar-policy evidence exceeds this parent. Retire/rebind3F5605DDBB34(initialneutrality200) to CCFD03FFBD3B,2C2E364445DD(coalition202) to E1A9AD724C4E,and A26E8CE8B534(colonialshift/repression212) to51F0F6F76B36/DACCA6754DFE after verifying their reviewed replacements. Existing coherent subjects reportedly retain those exact distinctions; no loss should be inferred from a label alone. Keep211and215–218 negotiation sequence, with1796 refusal linked to Ireland planning, naval/financial shocks and the distinction between European gains and colonial restitution demands. EVID-SUCC-01ABA3A831E4 at218 should focus on Camperdown/continuing British strength; the actual break is narrated217. Parent already captures the main peace conditions accurately.

rows.label: Levy of 300,000 and resistance to conscription
rows.source_grounded_note: Levy300000: pages204,224,226,229,242 support the limited February levy, quotas/lots, exemptions, partial recruitment and regional resistance. Major warranted and properly separate from August mobilization. EVID-SUCC-4E69FF624188 on229 should distinguish reported provincial riots from signs of resistance inParis, not assert a Paris riot there. The main may name town-office/NationalGuard exemptions as the source’s concrete unequal-burden mechanism if these remain required. The federalist unwillingness to serve far fromhome is a contextual comparison, not proof that its departmental armies were identical to the national levy.

rows.label: Levée en masse and Carnot’s organization
rows.source_grounded_note: Levée en masse: pages204–206,248,250 support popular petitions, differentiated universal requisition, actual military eligibility, nominal versus equipped numbers, Carnot’s role and makeshift organization. Essential warranted by the source’s unprecedented national-mobilization argument. Main and stance appropriately distinguish duty types and actual conscription from radical universal-enlistment expectations. EVID-SUCC-CA056FD20981 on206 is general military-rebuilding context, not a distinct named personal act byCarnot; narrow wording accordingly. Keep Februarylevy in204as explicit antecedent, not as the same August decree. Concrete women/children/olderpeople duties may be stated in parent meaning to avoid access aliases becoming the only carriers of this requirement.

rows.label: Free people of colour: colonial citizenship and successive rights decisions
rows.source_grounded_note: Free people of colour: pages150–151,411–412 support representation and white opposition, violent suppression, Robespierre/Barnave political contest and May1791 limited-parentage rights followed byApril1792 extension. Major warranted. Main should preserve the metropolitan political effect, including Robespierre’s enhancedstanding, if that nested treatment remains required. The current parent correctly separates free people’s citizenship from slavery/emancipation. Page411’s suppression sentence continues412withOgé’s name/fate, already included in the evidence set. Do not turn the broad151victory into unqualified universal rights in1791.

rows.label: Saint-Domingue slave uprising and colonial crisis
rows.source_grounded_note: Slave uprising: pages181,412 support colonial conflict, delayed policy communications, metropolitan antislavery/commercial tensions and the uprising driving later racial policy. Major warranted alongside the distinct essential emancipation/independence outcomes. Main immediate commodity-price consequences should be made chronological: reports arrivedOctober/December and severe sugar shortages/price-setting appearedJanuary1792; not instantaneousAugust transmission. Source identifies its historical superlative; preserve attribution rather than independently claiming it as a general world-history conclusion. Add CHUNK-017 to chapter provenance and correct physical source_chunk_id for90E264487B0D. Its existing treatment/facet includes412, so no new substantive claim is needed merely to repair provenance.

rows.source_grounded_note: Civil Code: pages385,389,407 support active codification using earlier papers, legal clarity and property transmission, later consolidation of landowners’rights and resistance to expeditedlegislation. Revise meaning to distinguish Code rules/consolidation from theConcordat/propertysettlement, and retain the interaction in appropriate relationship/task. Add CHUNK-017 provenance/source tag and407to treatment/facet pages for9BBA2028CF87. The inheritance/transmission summary407is supportable. Include legislative obstruction as political context, preserving389chronology uncertainty.

rows.label: Toussaint L'Ouverture, restored slavery, and Haitian independence
rows.source_grounded_note: Toussaint/Haiti: pages412–413 support alliances, blackmilitaryauthority, Britishinterventionandwithdrawal, autonomy, capture, disease, restorationnews, renewedresistance andwar, independence andpostindependenceviolence. Essential warranted as the distinct independent-state outcome. Main preserves failure to restore slavery inSaintDomingue versus restorationelsewhere, and qualified formalFrenchloyalty. It should explicitly retain Dessalines’s later massacre/imperialproclamation if the corresponding access route remainsrequired, not hide it behind generic priorracialconflict. Evidence413can expand to state this supportedaftermath. British13000deaths belong to the separatelyreviewedcolonialstrategyrequirement; do not merge them with Frenchdiseaselosses or infer a commondeathcount.
